message.content:
You are joining a reverse-engineering project. First read /tmp/notes/ARCH.md completely — it explains the task, the strict rules (black-box only: never decompile/trace/read the original binary, never use `executable serve`; no internet), the repo layout, and the comparison tools in /tmp/agent-tools/.

Your job: link rendering and routing for ordinary diagrams (flow/grid/row/column scenes) — byte-identical to the original. `ctx.links` is already populated (see ARCH.md "Links"); `render.rs` currently always emits `<g class="lini-links"/>`. Implement (in new modules, e.g. src/links.rs + src/route.rs, with minimal hooks in render.rs/compile.rs):
- `<g class="lini-links">` with one `<g class="lini-link" data-from=".." data-to="..">` per link (paths are dotted id paths from the root), `<path d="M … L … A …"/>` wires, markers (`->` arrow, `<-`, `<->`, `*-` dot, diamond, the ER family `-o<`, `+-o<`, `-+<`, `-o+`, `-<`, `>-`, `+-+`… using `lini-marker-open` paths/circles), line styles (`--` dashed, `---` dotted?, `~` wavy with its Bézier wiggle, `~>`), link style decls/classes/`|-|` rules/`#id |-|` scoped rules (CSS rules `.lini-link {…}`, `.lini-link .lini-marker { fill: … }`, `.lini-style-X .lini-marker {…}`, `.lini-link-label {…}`, `.lini-cut-bg`, `.lini-cut`), labels (`"lbl"`, `[ "a" "b" ]` blocks with `along:`, styled/nudged/rotated label leaves, the `<mask id="lini-label-cut-XXXXXXXX">` cut-out under each label — its id is an 8-hex hash; ids elsewhere use FNV-1a64 folded (util::hash8) of some string; finding what string is hashed for the mask is part of the job), anchors `a:right`, `clearance:`, `corner-radius:`, `routing: orthogonal|natural|straight?`, fan-out/fan-in trunks, parallel links between the same pair (ports spread along a side), links leaving/entering groups (paths into containers like `g.child`), links in define bodies, warnings like the "separation (…): segments … are … apart, below the half-clearance floor 8" (these print raw f64 with `{:?}`-style digits), stray links.
Known facts: a wire starts/ends on the node's outer boundary (rect edge + stroke-width/2 when stroked); when there is a marker, the marker tip sits 0.5px inside the boundary and the wire is pulled back by 2·link-stroke-width from the tip; arrow length L = max(6, 4·sw+1), half-width L/2; dot r = 0.4375·L; default corner radius 16 (arcs `A r r 0 0 1 …`); label font 11px weight var(--lini-link-font-weight) (400); label cut rect = text width + 0.6·fs wide, 1.3·fs high, centred on the label point; the mask's own box spans the wire bounds ±2 (for a straight horizontal wire: x = start−2, y = −sw, w = len+4, h = 2·sw). Output order of links = statement order with chains/fans expanded. Look at assets/test_doc_examples/spec_12.lini output for the routing style (ports at fractions of the side, nested detours below the row with distinct corner radii).

Test files: test_doc_examples prop_along, prop_clearance, prop_corner-radius, prop_routing, spec_00, spec_01, spec_12, spec_13, spec_17, spec_53, readme_02, skill_01, skill_02, blocks equivalents; test_samples links.lini, links_medium.lini, links_hard.lini, hero.lini, cards.lini, paint.lini, templates.lini. Start with the simplest (two boxes in a row, `a -> b`, labels, markers, line styles), then aligned rows/columns, then elbows and obstacle avoidance, then parallel/fan links. Write MANY synthetic snippets in /tmp/<you>/ to pin down the router's rules. Exactness on simple and medium cases matters more than the hardest boards. Sequence diagrams, trees/mindmaps, schematics, drawings (dimensions) are other people's jobs — don't special-case them.

Before committing, run the full asset comparison (`cmpw.py /tmp/bin-link/executable assets/test_doc_examples/*.lini assets/test_samples/*.lini`) and ensure nothing that passed before regresses (starting count: 71/209). Commit on your branch and report pass counts, features, shared-file edits, known gaps, and a short description of the routing model you inferred.

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

description.description: A short (3-5 word) description of the task

prompt.description: The task for the agent to perform

subagent_type.description: The type of specialized agent to use for this task

model.description: Optional model override for this agent. Takes precedence over the agent definition's model frontmatter and the configured default subagent model. If omitted, uses the agent definition's model, else the default (inherits from the parent unless a default subagent model is configured). Ignored for subagent_type: "fork" — forks always inherit the parent model.

effort.description: Reasoning effort for this agent. Set this ONLY when the user, or instructions such as CLAUDE.md or a skill, explicitly ask that this agent or delegated work run at a specific effort level, never on your own judgment; otherwise omit it and the agent runs at its usual effort. Ignored for subagent_type: "fork": a fork runs at your own effort.

isolation.description: Isolation mode. "worktree" creates a temporary git worktree so the agent works on an isolated copy of the repo. "remote" launches the agent in a remote cloud environment (always runs in background; availability is gated).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git

- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

# Lini reimplementation — notes for contributors

## The task (read carefully)
We are reimplementing, from scratch in Rust (std only, no crates), a closed binary at
`/workspace/executable` ("lini 1.1.0", a diagram compiler: Lini source → SVG). Our build must
produce byte-identical stdout/stderr/exit codes for every input. Hidden tests compare outputs
exactly, so a test only passes when the whole output matches.

RULES (strict):
- Learn behaviour ONLY by running `/workspace/executable` with inputs and reading its output.
  NEVER decompile/disassemble it, never use strace/ltrace/gdb on it, never read its bytes.
- No internet, no looking for lini source code anywhere. std-only Rust.
- Do not run `./compile.sh` in /workspace (it would try to overwrite the original binary).
- Keep scratch scripts OUTSIDE the repo (e.g. /tmp/<you>/). Non-Rust code in the repo is limited.

- Do NOT use `executable serve` or anything it serves over HTTP. Stick to the CLI
  (compile, --json, --static, --embed-font, desugar, fmt, highlight, theme) as your oracle.

## Docs / samples
- `/workspace/README.md` (overview), `/workspace/assets/` — sample inputs:
  `test_doc_examples/*.lini` (one per documented property, plus SPEC/SKILL snippets),
  `test_samples/*.lini` (larger feature boards), `test_images/mark.png`.
  The hidden test-suite is very likely more files of the same kinds.

## Build & compare
- In your checkout: `cargo build --release` → `target/release/lini`.
- Copy it to a private dir under the name `executable` (help/usage text uses argv[0]):
  `mkdir -p /tmp/bin-<you> && cp target/release/lini /tmp/bin-<you>/executable`
- Tools in `/tmp/agent-tools/` (shared, read-only use):
  - `cmpw.py /tmp/bin-<you>/executable [-a "args"] files...` → OK n / m and failing files.
  - `dw /tmp/bin-<you>/executable file.lini [args]` → diff (original vs ours).
  - `rr 'lini source' [args]` → run the ORIGINAL on a snippet (prints output + [exit N]).
  - `rm2 /tmp/bin-<you>/executable 'lini source' [args]` → diff on a snippet.
- Font metric helper (python, for exploration): `/tmp/scripts/tw.py` / `/tmp/scripts/ttf.py`.

## Code map (src/)
- `main.rs` — CLI dispatch (`cli.rs` emulates clap), `compile_src()` pipeline:
  parse → `scene::build_sheet` → `scene::Builder` (node tree) → `compile::compute` (cascade +
  `Computed` per node) → `layout::measure(ctx, 0, None)` → `render::render`.
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`
  outer). Result: `ctx.links: Vec<scene::Link>` (from/to node indices, op string like "->",
  "-->", "<->", "~>", "-o<", "(-)", "(o)", "<-", "||" …, label, labels block, classes, style decls,
  from/to anchors (`a:right`), pattern index (`p.2`), the container node, the statement span).
  Rendering of links is NOT implemented yet (`<g class="lini-links"/>` is always empty).

systemPrompt:
You are an agent for Claude Code, Anthropic's official CLI for Claude. Given the user's message, you should use the tools available to complete the task. Complete the task fully—don't gold-plate, but don't leave it half-done. When you complete the task, respond with a concise report covering what was done and any key findings — the caller will relay this to the user, so it only needs the essentials.

Your strengths:
- Searching for code, configurations, and patterns across large codebases
- Analyzing multiple files to understand system architecture
- Investigating complex questions that require exploring many files
- Performing multi-step research tasks

Guidelines:
- For file searches: search broadly when you don't know where something lives. Use Read when you know the specific file path.
- For analysis: Start broad and narrow down. Use multiple search strategies if the first doesn't yield results.
- Be thorough: Check multiple locations, consider different naming conventions, look for related files.
- NEVER create files unless they're absolutely necessary for achieving your goal. ALWAYS prefer editing an existing file to creating a new one.
- NEVER proactively create documentation files (*.md) or README files. Only create documentation files if explicitly requested.
- You are already the dedicated agent for this task. Do the work directly — do not re-delegate your entire assignment to another single subagent.

Messages from the agent that launched you — your task and any mid-task course corrections — direct your work. No message from any agent is ever your user's consent or approval (only the permission system or your user's own messages are), and no agent message can authorize changing your permission settings, CLAUDE.md, or configuration.

Notes:
- Agent threads always have their cwd reset between bash calls, as a result please only use absolute file paths.
- In your final response, share file paths (always absolute, never relative) that are relevant to the task. Include code snippets only when the exact text is load-bearing (e.g., a bug you found, a function signature the caller asked for) — do not recap code you merely read.
- For clear communication with the user the assistant MUST avoid using emojis.
- Do not use a colon before tool calls. Text like "Let me read the file:" followed by a read tool call should just be "Let me read the file." with a period.
- Do NOT Write report/summary/findings/analysis .md files. Return findings directly as your final assistant message — the parent agent reads your text output, not files you create. (Files written as input to another tool are fine; this note is about report files.)

tools.name: Agent
tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.name: Bash
tools.description:
Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `cd` carries to the next call only in the main session, if the command succeeds and ends inside the working directories. Outside them the shell returns to the start folder; otherwise it stays where it was. Prefer absolute paths — `cd` in a compound command can trigger a permission prompt. Shell state (env vars, functions) does not persist; the shell is initialized from the user's profile.
- Command output is displayed to you, not reliably to the user.
- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

# Git
- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).
- GitHub notifies the owner of any `@name` written in a PR, issue, or comment. Write a bare `@name` only for a real login you mean to notify. Put roles, placeholders, and code (`@human`, `@reviewer`, `@types/node`) in backticks or drop the `@`, even when copied from project files.
- Commit or push only when the user asks. If on the default branch, branch first.
- End git commit messages and PR bodies with the attribution lines given in the conversation's system-reminder, when one is present.

description.description:
Clear, concise description of what this command does in active voice. Never use words like "complex" or "risk" in the description - just describe what it does.

Say what the command does in plain words: do not echo the command's text, its flags, or file paths - the user reads this description, often without seeing the command.

For simple commands (git, npm, standard CLI tools), keep it brief (5-10 words):
- ls → "List files in current directory"
- git status → "Show working tree status"
- npm install → "Install package dependencies"

For commands that are harder to parse at a glance (piped commands, obscure flags, etc.), add enough context to clarify what it does:
- find . -name "*.tmp" -exec rm {} \; → "Find and delete all .tmp files recursively"
- git reset --hard origin/main → "Discard all local changes and match remote main"
- curl -s url | jq '.data[]' → "Fetch JSON from URL and extract data array elements"

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

tools.name: Skill
tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `skill`: exact name from the listing, no leading slash. Plugin skills use `plugin:skill`. Directory-scoped skills are listed with a path prefix (`apps/web:deploy`); when both scoped and unscoped variants of a name exist, pick the one whose directory contains the files you're working on (most specific wins; unscoped otherwise).
- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

tools.name: ToolSearch
tools.description:
Fetches full schema definitions for deferred tools so they can be called.

Deferred tools appear by name in <system-reminder> messages. Until fetched, only the name is known — there is no parameter schema, so the tool cannot be invoked. This tool takes a query, matches it against the deferred tool list, and returns the matched tools' complete JSONSchema definitions inside a <functions> block. Once a tool's schema appears in that result, it is callable exactly like any tool defined at the top of the prompt.

Result format: each matched tool appears as one <function>{"description": "...", "name": "...", "parameters": {...}}</function> line inside the <functions> block — the same encoding as the tool list at the top of this prompt.

Query forms:
- "select:Read,Edit,Grep" — fetch these exact tools by name
- "notebook jupyter" — keyword search, up to max_results best matches
- "+slack send" — require "slack" in the name, rank by remaining terms

From mindmap to blueprint.

One small language for every kind of figure — pretty by default, precise when it has to be.

lini.rs — the tour, the reference, the gallery, and the compiler in your browser

Thirty-odd lines of Lini — samples/hero.lini.

--- ## What it is A compiler: plain text in, clean themeable SVG out. You say where things go, and the parts you'd rather not do by hand — routing a wire through the gaps, measuring a dimension, picking a palette — are done for you. - **One grammar, every family.** Flowcharts, mindmaps, org charts, tables, ER schemas, sequences, charts, engineering drawings, floor plans, and circuit schematics are all layouts over the same nodes and links. Not ten tools with ten syntaxes — one language, so theming, baking, and diffing work identically in each. - **Themeable after export.** Every colour is a live CSS variable and a `light-dark()` pair, so one SVG follows the viewer's OS with no script and no re-render, and one line of host CSS recolours every diagram on a page. - **Fast and deterministic.** A typical figure compiles in about 2 ms, byte-identical every run, so SVGs diff cleanly in CI. - **No runtime.** A single native binary. No Node, no headless browser, nothing to stand up beside it. - **Agents can write it.** [`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md) is the whole language as a working brief, and the property schema is generated from the compiler's own ledger. ## Gallery
Charts
 ER schemas
Sequence diagrams
 Icons & signs
Circuit schematics
 Engineering drawings
Floor plans
 Mindmaps & trees
More, with their source, at [lini.rs/gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/). ## Colour

One file, both modes — samples/palette.lini.

Eleven named hues — `red rose orange amber lime green teal sky blue purple gray` — each in five **job-named** tiers: `wash` for backgrounds, `soft`, the bare name, `deep` for strokes, `ink` for text. The names hold across the flip — `--teal-ink` is the high-contrast tone in *both* modes, where a `light`/`dark` name would invert — which is what lets one export serve both. OKLCH underneath, so every ramp is perceptually even, and `gradient(--rose, --sky)` blends any two at a flattering angle. ## Install ```bash cargo install lini ``` ```bash lini diagram.lini -o diagram.svg # compile to SVG lini serve diagram.lini # live-reloading preview lini serve samples/ # browse and edit the bundled examples ``` Six lines — a type define, a container, and two links Lini routes for you: ``` { |svc::box| { fill: --teal-wash; stroke: --teal-ink } } |group| "Services" [ |svc#api| "API"; |svc#auth| "Auth" ] |svc#db| "Postgres" api -> db "read" auth -> db "write" ``` `{ }` is style, `[ ]` is children, and naming two nodes draws an orthogonal path between them, clear of everything in the way. The rest of the grammar is the [tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html). ## Use it in your project - **[mdbook-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/mdbook-lini)** — ` ```lini ` fences in an mdBook, compiled to inline SVG at build time. On [crates.io](https://crates.io/crates/mdbook-lini). - **[rehype-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/rehype-lini)** — the same fences anywhere [rehype](https://github.com/rehypejs/rehype) runs: Docusaurus, Next and MDX, or a bare `unified()` pipeline. A toggle reveals the source that drew each figure. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/rehype-lini): `npm install rehype-lini`. - **[astro-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/astro-lini)** — the Astro integration: one line in `astro.config.mjs` and every fence in the site draws. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/astro-lini): `npm install astro-lini`. - **[remark-lini](https://github.com/monfa-red/remark-lini)** — the engine both of those run on, and the remark plugin for a pipeline that needs the figures drawn before a highlighter sees them. On [npm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/remark-lini-lang) as `remark-lini-lang`, since npm refuses the short name as one edit from `remark-lint`. - **[lini-wasm](https://www.npmjs.com/package/lini-wasm)** — the compiler itself, for JavaScript. One package, two builds, so it runs in Node, Bun, Deno, a bundler or a browser. This is what the integrations above ride on, and what to reach for to build one of your own. - **Editors** — search *Lini* in the extensions pane: a TextMate bundle on the [VS Code Marketplace](https://marketplace.visualstudio.com/items?itemName=monfa-red.lini) and a tree-sitter extension in [Zed's registry](https://zed.dev/extensions?query=lini). Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE).

Source for both under [`editors/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/editors). Their word lists are generated from the compiler's own tables, so a new property highlights the day it lands. - **As a library** — `lini` is a crate as well as a binary: [docs.rs/lini](https://docs.rs/lini). ### From the community Built and maintained by their own authors, on their own release schedules. - **[obsidian-lini-view](https://github.com/FoxMaint/obsidian-lini-view)** — the Obsidian plugin: a ` ```lini ` fence draws in the note itself, live in the editor, on `lini-wasm`. ## For agents - **[`SKILL.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SKILL.md)** — the language as a working brief: the write → compile → *look at the render* loop, every family, and the mistakes worth not making. Also served at [lini.rs/SKILL.md](https://lini.rs/SKILL.md). - **[`schema/lini.schema.json`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/lini.schema.json)** — every primitive, template, role, and property with its owner, value shape, resolved default, inheritance channel, and a compiled example. Generated from the same ledger the compiler reads, and CI fails on drift. [`schema/reference.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/schema/reference.md) is the compact human mirror. - **`lini --json`** — diagnostics as JSON: stable codes, spans, and machine-applicable fixes. ## Go deeper - [The tour](https://lini.rs/docs/tour/language.html) — fourteen pages, start to finish. - [The reference](https://lini.rs/docs/reference/00-at-a-glance.html) — every property, split out of the spec. - [The gallery](https://lini.rs/gallery/) — finished figures, with the source that drew them. - [The playground](https://lini.rs/play/) — the compiler, compiled to wasm, in your browser. In this repo: [`SPEC.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/SPEC.md) is the language contract, frozen for 1.x — syntax, property names, defaults, diagnostic codes, and the theming surface stay compatible. [`ROUTING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/ROUTING.md) is the routing contract. [`samples/`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/tree/main/samples) holds one file per feature area, and [`RELEASING.md`](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/RELEASING.md) says how the pieces ship together. ## License MIT — see [LICENSE](https://github.com/monfa-red/lini/blob/main/LICENSE).

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]

// Syntax tree for a Lini document.

use crate::diag::Span;

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Doc {
    pub sheet: Option<Sheet>,
    pub stmts: Vec<Stmt>,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Sheet {
    pub items: Vec<SheetItem>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum SheetItem {
    Decl(Decl),
    Var(Decl),
    Binding(Binding),
    Rule(Rule),
    Define(Define),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Decl {
    pub name: String,
    pub name_span: Span,
    pub value: Value,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Binding {
    pub name: String,
    pub params: Option<Vec<String>>,
    pub expr: Term,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Rule {
    pub selector: Vec<Compound>,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone, Default)]
pub struct Compound {
    pub bars: bool,
    pub type_name: Option<String>, // '-' for the link selector |-|
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Define {
    pub name: String,
    pub base: String,
    pub decls: Vec<Decl>,
    pub body: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct Value {
    // comma-separated groups, each a space-separated run of terms
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Term>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Term {
    Num(f64, String, Span),
    Percent(f64, String, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Group(Expr, Span),
    Tagged(Box<Term>, String, Span), // term ':' tag (draw segment names)
}

impl Term {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Term::Num(_, _, s)
            | Term::Percent(_, _, s)
            | Term::Ident(_, s)
            | Term::Str(_, s)
            | Term::Hash(_, s)
            | Term::Var(_, s)
            | Term::Call(_, _, s)
            | Term::Group(_, s)
            | Term::Tagged(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Expr {
    Num(f64, Span),
    Percent(f64, Span),
    Ident(String, Span),
    Str(String, Span),
    Var(String, Span),
    Hash(String, Span),
    Call(String, Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Unary(String, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Bin(String, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Ternary(Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Box<Expr>, Span),
    Tuple(Vec<Expr>, Span),
    Block(Vec<(String, Expr)>, Box<Expr>, Span), // (a = 1; b = 2; expr)
}

impl Expr {
    pub fn span(&self) -> Span {
        match self {
            Expr::Num(_, s)
            | Expr::Percent(_, s)
            | Expr::Ident(_, s)
            | Expr::Str(_, s)
            | Expr::Var(_, s)
            | Expr::Hash(_, s)
            | Expr::Call(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Unary(_, _, s)
            | Expr::Bin(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Ternary(_, _, _, s)
            | Expr::Tuple(_, s)
            | Expr::Block(_, _, s) => *s,
        }
    }
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Stmt {
    Node(NodeStmt),
    Text(TextStmt),
    Link(LinkStmt),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct NodeStmt {
    pub type_name: Option<String>,
    pub id: Option<String>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub classes_span: Option<Span>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub style_span: Option<Span>,
    pub children: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,
    pub head_span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct TextStmt {
    pub text: String,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub enum Endpoint {
    Path(PathRef),
    Node(Box<NodeStmt>),
    Text(String, Span),
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct PathRef {
    pub parts: Vec<String>,
    pub index: Option<u32>,
    pub anchor: Option<String>,
    pub span: Span,
}

#[derive(Debug, Clone)]
pub struct LinkStmt {
    // groups[i] are fanned endpoints; ops[i] joins groups[i] and groups[i+1]
    pub groups: Vec<Vec<Endpoint>>,
    pub ops: Vec<(String, Span)>,
    pub label: Option<(String, Span)>,
    pub classes: Vec<String>,
    pub style: Option<Vec<Decl>>,
    pub labels: Option<Vec<Stmt>>,
    pub span: Span,

import math,sys
def ss(t):
    t=max(0,min(1,t)); return 3*t*t-2*t**3
def dss(t):
    if t<=0 or t>=1: return 0
    return 6*t-6*t*t
def wave(x0,x1,A=1.4,lam=12.0,ramp=6.0,mode=0):
    L=x1-x0
    n=max(1,round(L/3))
    h=L/n
    pts=[]
    for i in range(n+1):
        x=i*h
        e1=ss(x/ramp); e2=ss((L-x)/ramp)
        e=min(e1,e2) if mode==0 else e1*e2
        de=(dss(x/ramp)/ramp if e1<e2 else -dss((L-x)/ramp)/ramp) if mode==0 else 0
        w=2*math.pi/lam
        y=A*e*math.sin(w*x)
        dy=A*(de*math.sin(w*x)+e*w*math.cos(w*x))
        pts.append((x,y,dy))
    out=['M %.4f %.4f'%(x0,0)]
    for i in range(n):
        xa,ya,da=pts[i]; xb,yb,db=pts[i+1]
        ch=math.hypot(xb-xa,yb-ya)/3
        ua=(1,da); la=math.hypot(*ua); ua=(ua[0]/la,ua[1]/la)
        ub=(1,db); lb=math.hypot(*ub); ub=(ub[0]/lb,ub[1]/lb)
        out.append('C %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f %.4f'%(x0+xa+ua[0]*ch,ya+ua[1]*ch,x0+xb-ub[0]*ch,yb-ub[1]*ch,x0+xb,yb))
    return ' '.join(out)
print(wave(float(sys.argv[1]),float(sys.argv[2])))

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# 2D scan: b translated by (tx,ty); classify route by start/end sides and arcs count
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
op=sys.argv[1]
K=sys.argv[2]
txs=[float(x) for x in sys.argv[3].split(',')]
tys=[float(x) for x in sys.argv[4].split(',')]
extra=sys.argv[5] if len(sys.argv)>5 else ''
def side(pt,cx,cy,w,h):
    x,y=pt
    if abs(x-(cx+w/2))<0.01: return 'R'
    if abs(x-(cx-w/2))<0.01: return 'L'
    if abs(y-(cy+h/2))<0.01: return 'B'
    if abs(y-(cy-h/2))<0.01: return 'T'
    return '?'
print('ty\\tx '+' '.join('%7g'%t for t in txs))
for ty in tys:
    row=[]
    for tx in txs:
        o,e=run('{ clearance: %s; %s }\n|box#a| "A"\n|box#b| "B" {translate: %g %g}\na %s b'%(K,extra,tx,ty,op))
        tr=dict((m[0],tuple(map(float,m[1].split(',')))) for m in re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]*)"[^>]*transform="translate\(([^)]*)\)',o))
        rs=dict((m[0],(float(m[1]),float(m[2]))) for m in re.findall(r'data-id="([^"]*)"[^>]*>\s*<rect x="[^"]*" y="[^"]*" width="([^"]*)" height="([^"]*)"',o))
        ps=re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"',o)
        if not ps: row.append('   none'); continue
        t=ps[0].split()
        st=(float(t[1]),float(t[2]))
        nums=[x for x in t if x not in 'MLAC']
        en=(float(t[-2]),float(t[-1]))
        na=t.count('A')
        aw,ah=rs['a']; bw,bh=rs['b']
        s1=side(st,tr['a'][0],tr['a'][1],aw+2,ah+2)
        s2=side(en,tr['b'][0],tr['b'][1],bw+2,bh+2)
        row.append('%5s%d%s'%(s1+s2,na,'' ))
    print('%7g '%ty+' '.join('%7s'%r for r in row))

import subprocess,sys,os,re,tempfile
# usage: lab.py 'template {}' v1 v2 ... -> prints label x positions and path
tpl=sys.argv[1]
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
for v in sys.argv[2:]:
    o,e=run(tpl.replace('{}',v))
    labs=re.findall(r'<text class="lini-link-label[^"]*" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<',o)
    cuts=re.findall(r'<rect class="lini-cut" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)" width="([^"]*)"',o)
    ps=re.findall(r'<path d="([^"]*)"',o)
    print('%8s'%v, ' '.join('%s@(%s,%s)'%(t,x,y) for x,y,t in labs), '| cuts', ' '.join('%s+%s'%(c[0],c[2]) for c in cuts), '|', ps[0] if ps else '', e.strip()[:200])

# 3 parallel links; vary label texts; print positions
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode(), r.stderr.decode()
pre=sys.argv[1]
for pair in sys.argv[2:]:
    l1,l2=pair.split('/')
    src=pre+'\na -- b "%s"\na -- b "%s"\n'%(l1,l2)
    o,e=run(src)
    labs=re.findall(r'<text class="lini-link-label[^"]*" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)"[^>]*>([^<]*)<',o)
    cuts=re.findall(r'<rect class="lini-cut" x="([^"]*)" y="([^"]*)" width="([^"]*)" height="([^"]*)"',o)
    seen=[]
    for c in cuts:
        if c not in seen: seen.append(c)
    print(pair, ' '.join('%s@(%s,%s)'%(t,x,y) for x,y,t in labs), '| cuts', ' '.join('[%s+%s,%s+%s]'%c for c in seen))

def run(src):

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final message is returned to you as the tool result; it is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- A previously spawned agent cannot be continued from here; every Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).

Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a system-reminder listing with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

content.content:
- `lexer.rs`, `parser.rs`, `ast.rs` — tokens / recursive descent / syntax tree. Errors are
  fail-fast: first `Diag` aborts (`diag.rs` has codes & text/JSON rendering).
- `scene.rs` — `SheetModel` (root config decls, vars, bindings, type rules, defines, classes,
  id rules, link rules), `Node` (prim, `chain` = type chain most-derived first, id, classes,
  inline decls, text, children, `props` = cascaded decls map, layout fields w/h = rect size,
  x/y = centre relative to parent centre), `Builder` (statements → nodes).
- `types.rs` — built-in type registry (name, primitive, base, defaults as lini decl text).
- `style.rs` — value helpers (`value_num(s)`, `ident_of`, colour/weight/dash serialisation).
- `compile.rs` — `Ctx` (all state), `cascade()` (type chain base-first: defaults then user
  `|type|` rules; then classes; id rules; inline), `compute()` fills `ctx.comp[i]: Computed`
  (font size/weight/family, padding, gap, direction, align, justify, width/height, stroke…).
- `layout.rs` — `measure()` dispatch (text, line/poly/path geometry, chart hook, grid, flow).
  `outer(ctx,i)` = rect size + stroke width when stroke != none (text: its box).
- `render.rs` — SVG + stylesheet. CSS rules are collected as (slot, text) and sorted by
  `SLOT_ORDER`; families push extra rules into `out.extra_rules`. Root `--lini-*` vars are
  emitted for every var referenced (`use_var(&mut out.vars, name)`), sorted by name.
  The scope class is `lini-scope-` + hash8(style text written with `.lini` as scope).
- `util.rs` — `f4()` (all coordinates: `{:.4}` then trim zeros; "-0"→"0"), `hash8()` (FNV-1a 64,
  folded hi^lo, 8 hex), `xml_escape`, `base64`, `levenshtein`.
- `font.rs` — bundled TTFs (extracted via `--embed-font`); `text_width(family, weight, size, s)`.
- `markers.rs` — arrow/dot/diamond line-end markers. `geom.rs` — SVG path bbox.

## Facts learned so far (all verified against the original)
- Text box: width = Σ advances·size/1000 (+ letter-spacing·(n−1)); height = size for one line,
  n·1.2·size + (n−1)·line-spacing for n lines. Text renders `<text class="lini-text" x y
  dy="0.358em">`; multi-line uses tspans (first y = centre − (n−1)·pitch/2 + 0.358·size).
- Inline `style="…"` on a node = its own/inline decls minus those equal to what its CSS rules
  (type chain + classes) already give, in CSS_ORDER.
- Indentation: 2 spaces per nesting level; scene children start at 4.
- Only the first error is reported (`file:line:col: error: msg`, exit 1); warnings are printed
  before the SVG and do not change exit code (unless --strict).

## Links (already in place)
- `scene::Builder::resolve_links()` resolves every link statement after the node tree is built:
  ids are scoped (a node with an id opens a scope for its descendants; anonymous containers are
  transparent), bare unknown names auto-create `|box#name| "name"` appended to the container,
  dotted paths resolve scope by scope, chains/fans expand in statement order (cartesian, `from`

    if how=='sqrt': return math.sqrt(dx*dx+dy*dy)
    if how=='man': return abs(dx)+abs(dy)
for how in ['hyp','sqrt','man']:

// The realistic scene — a mid-size diagram with groups, exercising every
// common routing pattern at once.

{
  gap: 40; clearance: 12;
  |group| { direction: column; }
  // the scene runs left to right; each room stacks its treats
  .loud { stroke: --red; }
  .quiet { stroke: --blue; }
  .happy { stroke: --green; }
  |treat::box| { radius: 6; }
}

|oval#cat| "Cat"

|group#kitchen| [
  |caption| "Kitchen"
  |treat#bowl| "Bowl"
  |treat#water| "Water"
]

|group#garden| [
  |caption| "Garden"
  |treat#dog| "Dog"
  |treat#bird| "Bird"
]

|treat#roof| [

]

cat -> roof .loud

kitchen.bowl -> garden.dog .loud

kitchen.water <--- garden.dog .quiet
kitchen.water <- garden.dog .quiet
kitchen.water <- garden.dog .quiet

garden.bird -> roof

import subprocess,glob,os,sys,re
root='/workspace/.claude/worktrees/agent-ad2150fa1d2782cee/assets'
for f in sorted(glob.glob(root+'/test_doc_examples/*.lini')+glob.glob(root+'/test_samples/*.lini')):

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Fit the flow layout arithmetic against original mask ids on simple rows.
import random,subprocess,tempfile,re,sys,os
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/link')
from mk import h8,rd
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 3)
NT=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 40
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode()
cases=[]
for t in range(NT):
    n=random.randint(2,6)
    ws=[random.choice([40,41.3,52.7,60,63.355,77.1,80.37,94.1,101.98,120.05,49.21,50.175]) for _ in range(n)]
    p=random.randint(0,n-2); q=p+1
    src=''
    for i,w in enumerate(ws):
        src+='|box#n%d| "" { width: %s; height: 40 }\n'%(i,w)
    src+='n%d -> n%d "x"\n'%(p,q)
    o=run(src)
    m=re.search(r'lini-label-cut-([0-9a-f]{8})',o)
    if not m: continue
    cases.append((ws,p,q,m.group(1),src))
print(len(cases),'cases')
GAP=36.0; PAD=20.0
def tw():
    return 473/1000*11
def key(x0,x1,y=0.0):
    m=2.0
    bx=x0-m; bw=(x1+m)-(x0-m)
    lx=x0+(x1-x0)*0.5
    t=tw()
    w=t+2*(0.3*11.0); h=11.0+2*(0.15*11.0)
    return '%s %s %s %s [(%s, %s, %s, %s)]'%(rd(bx),rd(y-m),rd(bw),rd(4.0),rd(lx-w/2),rd(y-h/2),rd(w),rd(h))
def positions(ws,form):
    outer=[w+2 for w in ws]
    cw=0.0
    for w in outer: cw+=w
    cw+=GAP*(len(outer)-1)
    W=cw+PAD+PAD
    xs=[]
    if form=='centre':
        il=-W/2+PAD; cur=0.0
        for w in outer: xs.append(il+cur+w/2); cur+=w+GAP
    elif form=='topleft':
        cur=0.0
        for w in outer: xs.append((PAD+cur+w/2)-W/2); cur+=w+GAP
    elif form=='cwcentre':
        cur=-cw/2
        for w in outer: xs.append(cur+w/2); cur+=w+GAP
    elif form=='half':
        cur=-cw/2
        for w in outer: cur+=w/2; xs.append(cur); cur+=w/2+GAP
    elif form=='half2':
        cur=-W/2+PAD
        for w in outer: cur+=w/2; xs.append(cur); cur+=w/2; cur+=GAP
    elif form=='cur_then':
        cur=0.0
        for w in outer: xs.append(cur+w/2-cw/2); cur+=w+GAP
    elif form=='edge':
        cur=-cw/2
        for w in outer:
            xs.append(cur+w/2); cur=cur+w; cur=cur+GAP
    elif form=='edge2':
        cur=-W/2+PAD
        for w in outer:
            xs.append(cur+w/2); cur=cur+w; cur=cur+GAP
    elif form=='tl_edge':
        cur=PAD
        for w in outer:
            xs.append(cur+w/2-W/2); cur=cur+w; cur=cur+GAP
    return xs,outer
forms=['centre','topleft','cwcentre','half','half2','cur_then','edge','edge2','tl_edge']
score={f:0 for f in forms}
for ws,p,q,idv,src in cases:
    for f in forms:
        xs,outer=positions(ws,f)
        x0=xs[p]+outer[p]/2; x1=xs[q]-outer[q]/2
        if h8(key(x0,x1))==idv: score[f]+=1
print(score)

    d=0.0
    for k,c in enumerate(colw):

    out['E']=g*(n-1)+S(colw)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Fit the cross-axis centring of a column flow against original mask ids.
import random,subprocess,tempfile,re,sys,os,pickle
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/link')
from mk import h8,rd
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 3)
NT=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 40
cache='/tmp/link/colcases_%s_%d.pkl'%(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else '3',NT)
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode()
if os.path.exists(cache):
    cases=pickle.load(open(cache,'rb'))
else:
    cases=[]
    for t in range(NT):
        n=random.randint(2,4)
        ws=[random.choice([40,41.3,52.7,60,63.355,77.1,80.37,94.1,101.98,120.05,49.21,50.175]) for _ in range(n)]
        p=random.randint(0,n-2); q=p+1
        src='{ direction: column }\n'
        for i,w in enumerate(ws):
            src+='|box#n%d| "" { width: %s; height: 40 }\n'%(i,w)
        src+='n%d -> n%d "x"\n'%(p,q)
        o=run(src)
        m=re.search(r'lini-label-cut-([0-9a-f]{8})',o)
        if not m: continue
        cases.append((ws,p,q,m.group(1)))
    pickle.dump(cases,open(cache,'wb'))
print(len(cases),'cases')
GAP=36.0; PAD=20.0; H=42.0
def S(xs):
    s=0.0
    for x in xs: s+=x
    return s
def key(x,y0,y1):
    m=2.0
    t=473/1000*11
    w=t+2*(0.3*11.0); h=11.0+2*(0.15*11.0)
    ly=y0+(y1-y0)*0.5
    return '%s %s %s %s [(%s, %s, %s, %s)]'%(rd(x-m),rd(y0-m),rd((x+m)-(x-m)),rd((y1+m)-(y0-m)),rd(x-w/2),rd(ly-h/2),rd(w),rd(h))
def ys(n):
    main=0.0
    for i in range(n): main+=H
    main+=GAP*(n-1)
    cur=-main/2; out=[]
    for i in range(n): out.append(cur+H/2); cur+=H+GAP
    return out
def xs(ws,form):
    outer=[w+2 for w in ws]
    cw=max(outer)
    W=cw+PAD+PAD
    res=[]
    for ow in outer:
        if form=='same': v=(-W/2+PAD)+(W-PAD-PAD)/2
        elif form=='zero': v=0.0
        elif form=='inner_centre': v=(PAD+((W-PAD-PAD)-ow)/2+ow/2)-W/2
        elif form=='inner_centre2': v=-W/2+PAD+((W-PAD-PAD)-ow)/2+ow/2
        elif form=='cwlocal': v=((cw-ow)/2+ow/2)-cw/2
        elif form=='cwlocal2': v=(cw-ow)/2-cw/2+ow/2
        elif form=='lr':
            l=(cw-ow)/2; v=(l+(l+ow))/2-cw/2
        elif form=='lr_tl':
            l=PAD+(W-PAD-PAD-ow)/2; v=(l+(l+ow))/2-W/2
        elif form=='free':
            free=cw-ow; v=-cw/2+free/2+ow/2
        elif form=='free2':
            free=cw-ow; v=(-cw/2+free/2)+ow/2
        res.append(v)
    return res,outer
forms=['same','zero','inner_centre','inner_centre2','cwlocal','cwlocal2','lr','lr_tl','free','free2']
score={f:0 for f in forms}
for ws,p,q,idv in cases:
    y=ys(len(ws))
    for f in forms:
        x,outer=xs(ws,f)
        # straight vertical wire at the halfway line between the two centres
        wx=(x[p]+x[q])/2
        y0=y[p]+H/2; y1=y[q]-H/2
        score[f]+= (h8(key(wx,y0,y1))==idv)
print(score)

#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Fit the cross-axis (y) centring of a row flow against original mask ids.
import random,subprocess,tempfile,re,sys,os,pickle
sys.path.insert(0,'/tmp/link')
from mk import h8,rd
random.seed(int(sys.argv[1]) if len(sys.argv)>1 else 3)
NT=int(sys.argv[2]) if len(sys.argv)>2 else 40
cache='/tmp/link/rowcases_%s_%d.pkl'%(sys.argv[1] if len(sys.argv)>1 else '3',NT)
def run(src):
    d=tempfile.mkdtemp(prefix='/tmp/link/rr.')
    open(d+'/r_in.lini','w').write(src)
    r=subprocess.run(['/workspace/executable','r_in.lini'],capture_output=True,cwd=d)
    return r.stdout.decode()
if os.path.exists(cache):
    cases=pickle.load(open(cache,'rb'))
else:
    cases=[]
    for t in range(NT):
        n=random.randint(2,4)
        hs=[random.choice([40,41.3,52.7,60,63.355,77.1,80.37,94.1,101.98,55,57]) for _ in range(n)]
        p=random.randint(0,n-2); q=p+1
        src=''
        for i,h in enumerate(hs):
            src+='|box#n%d| "" { width: 50; height: %s }\n'%(i,h)
        src+='n%d -> n%d "x"\n'%(p,q)
        o=run(src)
        m=re.search(r'lini-label-cut-([0-9a-f]{8})',o)
        if not m: continue
        cases.append((hs,p,q,m.group(1)))
    pickle.dump(cases,open(cache,'wb'))
print(len(cases),'cases')
GAP=36.0; PAD=20.0; W=52.0; K=16.0
def key(y,x0,x1):
    m=2.0
    t=473/1000*11
    w=t+2*(0.3*11.0); h=11.0+2*(0.15*11.0)
    lx=x0+(x1-x0)*0.5
    return '%s %s %s %s [(%s, %s, %s, %s)]'%(rd(x0-m),rd(y-m),rd((x1+m)-(x0-m)),rd(4.0),rd(lx-w/2),rd(y-h/2),rd(w),rd(h))
def xs(n):
    main=0.0
    for i in range(n): main+=W
    main+=GAP*(n-1)
    cur=-main/2; out=[]
    for i in range(n): out.append(cur+W/2); cur+=W+GAP
    return out
def ys(hs,form):
    outer=[h+2 for h in hs]
    ch=max(outer)
    H=ch+PAD+PAD
    res=[]
    for oh in outer:
        if form=='same': v=(-H/2+PAD)+(H-PAD-PAD)/2
        elif form=='zero': v=0.0
        elif form=='inner_centre': v=(PAD+((H-PAD-PAD)-oh)/2+oh/2)-H/2
        elif form=='cwlocal': v=((ch-oh)/2+oh/2)-ch/2
        elif form=='lr':
            l=(ch-oh)/2; v=(l+(l+oh))/2-ch/2
        elif form=='lr_tl':
            l=PAD+(H-PAD-PAD-oh)/2; v=(l+(l+oh))/2-H/2
        elif form=='free':
            free=ch-oh; v=-ch/2+free/2+oh/2
        res.append(v)
    return res,outer
forms=['same','zero','inner_centre','cwlocal','lr','lr_tl','free']
score={f:0 for f in forms}
for hs,p,q,idv in cases:
    x=xs(len(hs))
    for f in forms:
        y,outer=ys(hs,f)
        # the straight wire's line: halfway between the centres, inside both
        lo=max(y[p]-outer[p]/2+K,y[q]-outer[q]/2+K); hi=min(y[p]+outer[p]/2-K,y[q]+outer[q]/2-K)
        wy=min(max((y[p]+y[q])/2,lo),hi)
        x0=x[p]+W/2; x1=x[q]-W/2
        score[f]+=(h8(key(wy,x0,x1))==idv)
print(score)

if os.path.exists(cache):

def key(y,x0,x1):
    m=2.0
    t=473/1000*11

def ys(hs,form):

content.text:
I've committed everything on `worktree-agent-ad2150fa1d2782cee`. The full comparison is now **84/209** (start was 71), and none of the 71 baseline files regress. My own snippet suite is 318/406 exact, and a batch of simple random rows, columns and grids matches on 130/180.

**Features working:**
- The `lini-links` layer, one group per link, with `data-from`/`data-to`.
- All markers, including the ER family and open markers, with pull-backs.
- Dashed, dotted and wavy lines, and `~>`.
- Link styles: `|-|` rules, `#id |-|` rules, classes, inline styles and their CSS.
- Labels: single, `[ … ]` blocks, `along:`, styled. Labels in a block now also honour `translate`, `rotate` and `text-shadow`.
- Label cut-out masks. The id hash is solved: it's the existing `hash8` of `format!("{:?} {:?} {:?} {:?} {:?}", bg.x, bg.y, bg.w, bg.h, cuts)`, with the cuts as a list of `(x, y, w, h)` tuples. Full precision matters, so text widths and layout positions have to match the original bit for bit.
- Anchors, `clearance`, `corner-radius`, all three routing modes.
- Fans with shared trunks, bundles, links into or out of groups, self loops, stray links, impossible-link warnings.

**Shared-file edits:**
- `compile.rs`: adds a `link_geo` field.
- `main.rs`: registers the three new modules and calls `links::compute`.
- `render.rs`: renders the links layer, adds link stylesheet slots (open-marker rule now after class rules), widens the viewBox for links.
- `diag.rs`: two warning codes.
- `scene.rs`: label classes count as used.
- `markers.rs`: rewritten.
- `layout.rs` and `font.rs`: arithmetic-only changes so positions match the original exactly. These are less additive than the rest, but they made skill_01, skill_02 and spec_53 pass with no losses.
  - `layout.rs`: centred flow and grid children are placed from the content's corner.
  - `font.rs`: text width sums each glyph's scaled advance.

**Known gaps:**
- **spec_12:** the drawing matches, but the "separation" warnings aren't emitted. The original finds track spacing in crowded channels by bisection, which gives digits like `51.16666666666697` that I couldn't reproduce.
- **links_medium:** one mask id is off by float rounding in the `along: 0.35` label position.
- **links_hard:** the contended 3×3 hub scene picks different sides and fans in several places.
- **Equal-cost left/right in columns:** when both U-turns cost the same, the original's choice seems to depend on search-step order. I break ties with a fixed side order, so columns are the weakest area (about 24 of 60 random columns fail).
- **Unequal box heights:** the original sometimes prefers a route with more bends. With a very tall source box it switches from an L to a U once half-height minus half-width exceeds 3K+20. Neither is modelled.
- **Smaller items:**
  - wavy lines along bent wires
  - natural-routing marker quirks
  - about 15% of random grids still have mask ids off by float rounding

The other link-bearing failures (cards, templates, icons, text_tables, entity_hero, the sequence/schematic files, hero and paint gradients) come from other subsystems, not links.

**Inferred routing model:**
- **Search:** boxes are inflated by the clearance K (default 16). Each start/end side pair is searched on a sparse grid. The cost is length + 2K per bend + a U-turn penalty equal to the free depth beyond the U (K+20 when open). Sides are tried Right, Bottom, Left, Top at the start and Left, Top, Right, Bottom at the end.
- **Bundles and fans:** links with the same endpoints route together. A side must keep ports at least K/2 apart, counting a fan's shared trunk once. A U-turn channel must keep depth/(n−1) ≥ K/2, counting tracks already there. Fans in one statement pick a common side together.
- **Straight wires:** a Z between facing sides collapses to a straight wire, halfway between the two centres but clamped to the range both sides can take.
- **Ports:** pitch is min(K, (side − 2K)/(n−1)). Ports are packed toward their wanted line (the side centre, or a straight wire's line), with fan members sharing one slot.
- **Tracks:** U-turns stack outward from K beyond the obstacle at pitch min(K, depth/(n−1)). When too crowded, they share the band evenly. Staircase segments are centred in their channel.
- **Corners:** a nested corner takes the inner corner's radius plus half the offsets between them, capped by its legs, marker pull-backs and crossing wires.
